title: Depression in adults: treatment and management
authors: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
funder: not stated in the guideline text or its PDF.
result: Less severe depression is defined as a PHQ-9 score below 16. Do not routinely offer antidepressant medication as first-line treatment for less severe depression; only offer it if that is the person's informed preference (1.5.3). For more severe depression, SSRIs are generally well tolerated, have a good safety profile and should be considered as the first choice for most people. When stopping an antidepressant, slowly reduce the dose to zero in a step-wise fashion, at each step prescribing a proportion of the previous dose (for example 50%), consider smaller reductions (for example 25%) as the dose becomes lower, agree the speed with the person, and recognise that withdrawal may take weeks or months to complete (1.4.16). Withdrawal symptoms usually go away within 1 to 2 weeks but can last longer, in some cases several weeks and occasionally several months (1.4.14).
